SAM 3D predicts a full 6-DoF pose for every object it reconstructs, alongside the geometry. This page shows that predicted orientation for all 64 recordings, and tests it against something we know for certain: the cup and the plate both stand on a level table, so each object's symmetry axis must point along gravity. The angle between the prediction and vertical is therefore the error, directly. Related: how the reconstructions are made · dynamic scene gallery.

The predicted axis on each object

ALL TILES: drag a tile to rotate · ⌘/ctrl-scroll to zoom

The prediction is decoded from SAM 3D's rotation output (wxyz quaternion, camera→object; its canonical frame is y-up, verified to 1.5° across independent runs) and mapped into the recording's gravity-aligned SLAM world. The measurement floor is the tilt of the plate normal as measured from our own ICP-registered cloud — our yardstick carries that much error itself, so the plate's prediction is close to as good as this test can resolve. The cup is a nearly isotropic 7 × 7 × 6.6 cm shape with no distinguishing features, so its orientation is close to ill-posed and the predictions are correspondingly poor. Positions are metric to roughly 10 cm after correcting a y-up/y-down convention flip; predicted scale runs ~13% high but is genuinely metric. Practical read: good enough to initialise a registration, not to replace one.
